newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police graduates to lose "royal" status.
newsitem.headline: HK police graduates to lose "royal" status.

text.p: Hong Kong's new police graduates cannot afford to get too comfortable in their freshly-issued uniforms.

In just 10 days time not only do they lose the word "Royal" from their titles but they also have to get out their sewing kit to replace their badges with the red bauhinia flower design of the new Beijing-controlled Hong Kong government.
Caps, shoulder insignia and buttons all will undergo the change.
Outgoing governor Chris Patten on Saturday attended the graduating ceremony for the final "royal" class of 1997.
When Beijing takes control of Hong Kong on July 1 the present Royal Hong Kong Police Force becomes simply the Hong Kong Police Force.
"The officers of the Hong Kong Police Force earned the reward of the 'Royal' title through their service to the territory," said Patten in an address to the 161 new police officers.
"I think Hong Kong has without question the finest police force in Asia and one of the best police forces in the world," he added.
"Some of my colleagues were worried that the new bauhinia badge will not look as prestigious as the Royal crown," said 21-year-old Chau Chi Hang, one of the graduates.
